findings.text: follow-on: compare_tiers marks a job failed whenever raw_total is None (line 359: 'not (raw_total is not None and ...)'), so an old flat-key raw file with no engine section -- every counter absent, and every tier built from it also absent -- is reported as a disagreement even though no totals disagree. The reviewed node reproduced this exactly: it labelled 10 old-format jobs 'failed', and the node's own fragment describes them correctly as 'the check reports that no agreement could be computed'. But plan rule 2 (retention block) reads 'the partitioned totals ... must be equal exactly. A job fails if any one window or any one counter differs' -- on that reading absent==absent is equal, so the 10 jobs would pass, whereas the shared tool that the retire-raw listing also uses makes them permanently ineligible for retirement. This is a plan/tooling question the node could not settle from its brief, not a defect it introduced: the node used the plan's own compare_tiers unchanged and reported its result faithfully. Recorded because those 10 raw files will never become eligible under the rule-2 check as written, and a decision is owed on whether that is intended.

follow_ons.text: The reviewed node's brief (FENCE — EVIDENCE) asked it to run the per-hour three-counter check on every candidate; it ran it on 36 of 54 and deferred 18 (check.md totals: 2 passed, 10 failed, 24 skipped, 18 deferred), because compare_tiers ingest cost far exceeded the plan's recorded 8.9 s/MB (the node measured 353 s for an 808 KB file, job 1271376). The deferral is documented in the fragment, the manifest checkpoint and the follow_ons, and the retire-raw listing runs the same check before any file becomes eligible, so no unsound deletion is licensed. Recorded as an incomplete per-job check rather than a defect: rule 2's per-job equality is unverified for those 18 jobs until the retire-raw listing runs, and the dependency is one node away.

The staged rebuilt tiers differ by sha256 from the record directory's installed compacted files even for passing jobs (rebuild_results.json: minute_differs=true, hour_differs=true for the two passed jobs 1278049 and 1278060), which is expected -- the rebuild is under the corrected compaction while the installed tiers predate it -- and the totals agree. This is a positive signal that the rebuild is not a no-op, but it means the staged tiers are a correction of the installed ones, not a byte-copy; a later reader should not treat 'differs' as a fault. No action owed by this node.
